editorial:
Picture a greedy billionaire who buys a beautiful bay to build luxury homes, not knowing it is home to a secret group of mermaids. That is the wild setup of The Mermaid, a big, silly, and surprisingly sweet comedy from director Stephen Chow. Deng Chao plays Xuan, the rich playboy who thinks money can fix everything, while Lin Yun is Shan, the awkward mermaid sent to kill him. Their chemistry is goofy and charming, and the movie mixes slapstick humor with a clear message about protecting nature. It is loud, colorful, and never takes itself too seriously, which makes it an easy watch for a fun movie night.

The jokes come fast, sometimes silly and sometimes clever, and the special effects are a mix of impressive and intentionally cartoonish. The story can feel uneven, and some gags drag on, but the heart keeps you invested. If you enjoy over-the-top comedies with a romantic twist, this one is for you. Stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for the best picture.
endingExplained: In the finale, Xuan learns the mermaids are real and tries to protect them, but the villainous Ruolan shoots him. Shan, in her true mermaid form, saves his life and heals him. The police arrest Ruolan, the bay project is canceled, and Xuan and Shan end up together. The movie closes on a happy note, with the mermaids safe and Xuan changed for the better.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves over-the-top comedies with heart and fantasy romance.
